monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady fever keeping the turnip from sliding into the thin air above. I stand by the Tired Wedge, feeling how it leans hard against the stack. It feels tired, yet the lean seems to hold the weight just enough. I set down a tree log small beside the wedge, a fresh piece of memory for a place that changes every night. I tell myself I am pressing down to stop the slip, trusting the lean to catch it all. The shovel waits nearby, heavy and real, while I wonder if the air above is truly empty or just waiting for a lid. I will keep pressing, letting the wedge do its tired work while the card hums on.

action.why: The wedge feels tired but the lean must hold, so I will press it down again while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the wedge down harder on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. The air above is thin, so I let the weight choose where to go. I tell myself the wedge is not sliding, only leaning, and I set down a new tree log small beside it to mark the spot.

remembered.text: Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under.
The wedge leans hard, a tired thing refusing to slide into the thin air.
I set the tree log small down, hoping it stops the slip while the card hums warm.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: The wedge leans hard; I trust the lean to hold.

moments.name: The Tired Stack
moments.say: I press the log down, trusting the lean to hold.

recalled.text: Your diary: "I stopped pressing to let the edge bite, but the slip still slides. I set wide planks to catch it instead."
